dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Toodaloo is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Toodaloo has not acclimated well to the shelter environment despite best efforts to keep him comfortable. He has displayed a concerning level of leash biting, kennel fighting, and kennel stress. When attempting to leash Toodaloo, he will bite and pull leads into the kennel and does not readily release for treats. He has been observed to lick the kennel door, bite on the kennel bars and pull on them while wailing, and excessive drool is often found in his kennel. Once out of the kennel, he immediately lunges and hard barks at other dogs as he exits or enters the room. In quieter settings, Toodaloo will check in with handlers, tolerate some petting, chase tennis balls, or engage with lick mats or snuffle mats. During his handling assessment, he was noted to chuff and lip curl on the knock portion. Medically, Toodaloo is underweight and his left canine tooth has a fracture that will possibly need removal.

Toodaloo was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home enviornment is unknown. Toodaloo has been mostly social with handlers in care, but has intermittently displayed fearfulness, including during his handling assessments. During the knock portion, he began chuffing and lip curling when the assistant returned to the office. When given time, he readily approaches handlers for treats and some petting. Toodaloo has recently begun kennel fighting and leash biting when being returned or taken out of the kennel. Due to these concerns, we recommend that Toodaloo be placed in an adult-only home through a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.
